questions.q: Why does Altucher say the traditional American dream no longer works?
a: Work is outsourced or automated, so a degree no longer guarantees a job
Housing has become too expensive for most young families
Young people no longer want to own homes or cars
The government stopped supporting small businesses
questions.why: Lesson 1 argues that almost everything can now be outsourced or done by technology, leaving many graduates unemployed.

questions.q: What event does the summary credit with bursting the American dream bubble?
a: The 2008 financial crisis
The end of the Second World War
The rise of the internet in the 1990s
The publication of the book in 2013
questions.why: The summary says the dream burst in 2008, when the financial crisis led companies to cut costs by cutting people.

questions.q: According to the summary, what keeps most people from controlling their own dreams?
a: Fear of what family, friends and customers will think
A lack of savings and starting capital
Not knowing which product to build first
Too many job offers from employers
questions.why: Lesson 2 says avoiding rejection is a powerful motivator, and that fear hands control of your choices to others.

questions.q: Which four areas does Altucher's daily practice cover?
a: Mental, physical, emotional and spiritual health
Career, money, family and community
Sleep, diet, exercise and work
Reading, writing, saving and giving
questions.why: Lesson 3 lists mental, physical, emotional and spiritual health as the four areas to improve a little each day.

questions.q: What daily habit does the author recommend for building ideas?
a: Writing down ten ideas, whether good or bad
Reading one chapter of a business book
Pitching one new client before noon
Reviewing yesterday's mistakes in a journal
questions.why: The summary says Altucher writes ten ideas a day, no matter their quality, as part of his daily practice.
